pr_title: become - stop using play context in more places
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
There are still a few locations that are getting the become vars from play context and this can miss some options that are become specific, i.e. `ansible_<plugin>_pass` may not work for all plugins as they are defined as a plugin option and not in play context.

There are still some plugins that still use play context, like synchronize and some network action plugins but they should be fixed in a separate PR as they could be a larger change.

Fixes https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/62367. Also fixes the become_pass var for runas to be the correct name.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
become

<!--- boilerplate: components_banner --->

The variables are not deprecated or overridden, they are different variables and IMO should not replace each other. If you look at the docs for the [sudo become plugin](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/plugins/become/sudo.html) you can see that `become_pass` has the following variables that can be set

* `ansible_become_password`
* `ansible_become_pass`
* `ansible_sudo_pass`

The order is important as variables listed higher up in the list have a lower precedence than ones lower in the list, i.e. the become plugin will use `ansible_sudo_pass` for the password if set and will ignore `ansible_become_pass` or `ansible_become_password`.

In saying that I've found 2 bugs so far with this priority not being respected and I will open a PR to fix it shortly.

this is ridiculous, what's the point of this? as if ansible wasn't already confusing with everything having a similar name

in top of that, you look up google and you find people suggesting to use one variable or the other, in the docs ansible_become_pass has disappeared too (not this doc but the original "become" doc) but it was there last year

yes, because I had copied a lot of the text from that page in local and many variables have completely changed


but please, if it's "by design", then it should be changed to be more logical

> this is ridiculous, what's the point of this? as if ansible wasn't already confusing with everything having a similar name

Not sure if I agree here, the ability to set multiple vars can be beneficial, especially in case of vars that conflict with other plugins. Typically we add at least 2 vars for a plugin option:

* `ansible_<plugin type>_<option name>`
* `ansible_<pluign name>_<option name>` - typically has a higher precedence than the above

This allows users to have a generic option that is typically the same across all plugin types, but also allow them to set a specific option for a specific plugin. An example for the latter scenario is if I am managing both Windows and Linux hosts and I want my become to be the Admin user, I can now set the following in my `group_vars/all.yml`

```
ansible_sudo_user: root
ansible_runas_user: Administrator
```

Ultimately you don't have to do this at all if you don't want but the choice is there for people who want it.

What makes this a bit more complicated is that historically the var was set as `ansible_sudo_pass` in pre v2 (before become was a thing), and `ansible_become_pass` before 2.8, and now finally `ansible_become_password`. The `ansible_become_pass` should still work for all and `ansible_sudo_pass` for the sudo plugin only as we need a way to preserve backwards compatibility. The change from `_pass` to `_password` was a community driven change to better align our password variables hence why the global docs were changed.

Lastly on this point, the plugin config table is a generic setup that works the same across all plugins that implement it. This allows us to keep the same behaviour across different plugins instead of the old way where each component could have been set differently.
